brief: GS argues S&P 500 earnings are over-earning, not in a bubble. EPS grew 51% in Q2 and 26% over four quarters, nearly half from AI investment. GS forecasts growth decelerating to 11% in 2027 (EPS $415) and 2028 ($460) as GDP growth offsets a fading AI tailwind, which flips from an 11pp boost this year to a marginal drag by 2028. Risks: semiconductor margins reverting from 70% to their 15-year average of 55% would cut earnings 10%, and mega-cap "other income" from equity stakes lifted Q2 earnings 12%, a distortion. Prices lag EPS and trade at a P/E discount to a macro model, so GS keeps a 12-month S&P 500 target of +14% to 8,700, driven by earnings, not multiples. Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 208.8%, net 48.8%. CTA supply is expected to cease and demand resume after SPX cleared a short-term threshold. AAII sentiment sits at 2026 lows, still needing time before re-risking. GS holds its $5,400/toz end-2027 gold forecast despite a Fed hike and an expected October hike, since 2027-28 rate cuts leave the terminal rate unchanged. Fair value drops to $4,650/toz on slower appreciation, not a lower terminal price, driven by central bank buying near 91 tonnes/month.
